Alex.confusing: Round 1: why Ellis's Eagle got no visitor info. I never figured out that a Floofer's hug explained it. I was also unsure how a hug interacts with a visit's results.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when the Owl, Eagle, Tit and Kookaburra reports all lined up and the table found the Sphinx. Banking four high cards in that win was satisfying too.
Alex.change: Give the Owl and Tit more useful information, or let the Kookaburra's result be checkable. A Meowfia player can easily dodge a role question without being caught, as happened with Blair and Finley in round 3.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I piled onto Ellis, who was Farm, and that cost my side the round and 2 cards. Ellis's hugged-Eagle story was plausible, so I should have said so and pushed suspicion toward Blair, who was the Floofer.

Blair.confusing: The Kookaburra result handling was unclear: I was never told my dawn report would hide a role, so I dodged a question I should have answered. I also didn't know whether a visit that hugged or confused me would still show up in my report.
Blair.fun: Round 1 was fun: as the Floofer I hugged Ellis, and the table pushed a bad Eagle story that got Ellis eggsecuted for Meowfia's win.
Blair.change: I would make dawn reports clearer about role results and confusion, so players aren't left guessing whether a dodge is a lie.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I falsely said my dawn report didn't show Finley's role, when I should have simply named the role I learned. Honestly reporting that Finley was the Floofer would have exposed the Meowfia and likely saved Blair and my Farm side.

Casey.confusing: How the Owl and Eagle reports interact with a Floofer's hug, and why Ellis's Eagle report was empty in round 1. It was hard to tell a hug from a lie.
Casey.fun: Round 2, where I was the lone Sphinx and tried to deflect while the table converged on me. The Kookaburra callout of Blair in round 3 was also fun.
Casey.change: Show a hugged player that they were hugged, or give Meowfia a bit more to do at night. As it stands, a lone Meowfia with no teammate to coordinate with has little to work with.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I threw my three highest cards (10, 11, 9) at Ellis and lost them all. I should have thrown fewer or lower cards, since the Eagle's hug story was plausible and my own evidence was weak.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle and Owl visit-counting, since visitors weren't always named and claims conflicted on who visited whom. Round 2's Blair +3 was also easy to misread as Blair's own visitors.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when Casey was eggsecuted as the Sphinx and the Farm table won with a 12-to-1 throw. Cross-checking the Eagle and Owl counts against each other was satisfying.
Drew.change: Make the dawn report show the visitor names and roles a Kookaburra learns, so players can't dodge a claim by saying the report didn't show it.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I joined the pile-on against Blair, a Farm Kookaburra, without verifying, and lost two cards. I should have thrown at Finley, the Floofer Meowfia, whose Hawk claim I had already cross-checked against my Eagle report.

Ellis.confusing: Round 1: my Eagle got no visitor info at all. I couldn't tell whether I was hugged or whether the report was just empty. That made my own claim look like a lie.
Ellis.fun: Round 2: banking 24 points in one throw after the table converged on Casey, the Sphinx, and I jumped from 3 to 26.
Ellis.change: Tell a player explicitly when they were hugged or blocked, even if the report is otherwise empty. Otherwise a hugged player can't tell a hug from a liar's story, and neither can the table.
Ellis.regret: In round 3 I threw 12 and 13 at Blair, who turned out to be Farm, and lost both cards. I should have thrown the 2s, kept the big cards, and let the others carry the vote. The consensus already had Blair eggsecuted, and a bigger throw wasn't needed.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle and Owl counts were hard to check because visitor claims often conflicted, and nobody could tell whether a zero-egg report meant no visit or a hug.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was satisfying: as the Kookaburra I learned Casey was the Sphinx, and the table converged on a correct throw.
Finley.change: Make visit counts and hugs easier to verify, so claims like Eagle and Owl reports can be checked against each other.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I threw at Casey, a Farm Falcon, on the strength of a shaky Eagle/Owl story. I should have backed Ellis's account, which the Owl report partly supported, and kept my cards out of that throw.
